task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req061-execution-error-handling.md against REQ-061's acceptance criteria. Read the design artefact directly. Pay particular attention to: (1) whether AC4's tension (only 2 of 5 named calling paths exist in shipped code) is handled by an explicit, reasoned interim proposal rather than silently assumed away, (2) whether the rewiring of REQ-049's and REQ-050's existing error paths into the new shared sink is concretely specified (not just asserted), (3) whether AC3 being already-satisfied by shipped REQ-048 code is verified against the actual code rather than taken on the design doc's word, (4) no implementation code leaked in.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-061 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element or an explicitly-flagged, reasoned open question (not a silent assumption)
No TBD/deferral language for any in-scope acceptance criterion
Function signatures fully specified with @spec-style types and error shapes

result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/req061-execution-error-handling.md in full and independently re-verified its load-bearing claims against real shipped code rather than the doc's own assertions. (1) merge_output_variables/2 (lib/letflow/engine.ex:1043) confirmed: on VariableMerge.merge/3's {:rejected, ...} it returns {:error, {:unexpected_variable_rejection, events}} from a bare Multi.run/3 step -- an Ecto.Multi.run/3 {:error, _} return unconditionally aborts and rolls back the whole transaction, so today nothing persists and instance_projections.status stays :active; no ERROR state, no EXECUTION_ERROR event exist anywhere pre-this-design. (2) dispatch_task_completion_hop_chain/2 (engine.ex:1056) confirmed: on Transition.transition/3's {:error, reason} it returns {:error, {:transition_failed, reason}}, same abort-the-whole-Multi outcome; Transition.transition_error()'s {:no_matching_edge, node_id, evaluated_conditions} member (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:140, built at lines 382/441) confirmed as the exact shape the design cites for REQ-050. Both (1) and (2) confirm the design's central premise -- REQ-049/REQ-050 today have NO persisted ERROR state, only abort-and-return-tuple -- against the real code, not the doc's word. (3) AC3: fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3 (engine.ex, complete_task/3's M2) confirmed to pattern-match nil -> :instance_not_found, %{status: :active} -> {:ok, _}, %{status: status} -> {:error, {:instance_not_active, status}} -- :error is not special-cased out, so an ERROR-status instance is already rejected today with a distinct, existing conflict tuple; complete_error()'s union already names {:error, {:instance_not_active, status :: :completed | :cancelled | :error}}, confirmed by direct read. This independently confirms the design's claim that AC3 is already satisfied by shipped REQ-048 code with no new logic needed. Also spot-checked instance_projection.ex: status enum and terminal?/1 (true only for :completed/:cancelled, false for :active and :error) confirmed as claimed, and cancel_instance/3 (engine.ex:1302) confirmed to already treat :error as cancellable via terminal?/1 reuse, matching design §7's cross-reference. Checked design against the 6 gate criteria: every REQ-061 AC maps to a concrete design element or an explicitly-flagged reasoned open question (AC4's 'at least three of five' tension is addressed head-on in §15 with a stated interim recommendation, not silently assumed or silently weakened); no TBD/deferral language found (grep clean); function signatures (append_multi/3, set_instance_error/2, merge_outcome_for/2, transition_outcome_for/2) carry full @spec-style types including error unions; cross-module dependencies enumerated in §13; the Jason.encode!/event_attrs pseudocode blocks in §9 are payload-shape illustrations matching the established req045/req049 design convention, not real function bodies -- no .ex/.exs implementation code present; open questions (OQ-1..OQ-7) are listed explicitly rather than silently resolved. No blocking gaps found.
result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (Step 2) for OTP-idiom/decision-record sign-off, with particular attention to design §15's AC4 interim reading (2-of-2-shippable-callers-today) and §5's Multi.merge branch-point rewiring of complete_task/3, both flagged by CODE-DESIGNER as the load-bearing non-obvious parts.
